subject: Trading
title: Strike Price and Expiration
description: A fast breakdown of Strike Price and Expiration for builders.

hook.text: Every option has two key terms: the price you can buy or sell at (strike) and the deadline (expiration).

buildup.text: The strike price is your set price. A $100 strike call lets you buy shares at $100, no matter the market price.

discovery.text: Expiration is the deadline. After that date, the option ceases to exist—it either has value or it's worthless.

twist.text: Options lose value as expiration approaches—time decay. An out-of-the-money option near expiry is nearly worthless.

climax.text: Strike and expiration together define the option's character. The same stock trades thousands of different options.

punchline.text: Price, deadline, decision. That's an option.

quiz.question: What happens to an option at expiration?
options: It either has value and is exercised, or expires worthless
